textbookText: 21. Stars twinkle. Why? Ans:- Stars twinkle because the light coming from them passes through different layers of the Earth’s atmosphere, which have varying densities. These layers bend the light unevenly, making the stars appear to change brightness and position continuously. 22. The sun appears on the horizon about two minutes before the actual sunrise. Why? Ans:- The sun appears on the horizon about two minutes before the actual sunrise because the light from the sun bends as it passes through the Earth’s atmosphere. This atmospheric refraction makes the sun appear slightly higher in the sky than it actually is, allowing us to see it even when it is still below the horizon. 23. Sunlight is refracted when it is passed through a prism. Why? Ans:- Sunlight is refracted when it passes through a prism because the prism is made of a denser medium that changes the speed of light. Different colours of light bend by different amounts, causing the sunlight to spread into a spectrum. 24. A convex lens converges light rays. Why? Ans:- A convex lens converges light rays because it is thicker at the middle and thinner at the edges, causing light rays to bend inward as they pass through it. Due to this shape, the refracted rays meet at a point called the principal focus. 25. Deficiency of vitamin A in the body one of the main causes of night blindness. Why? Ans:- Deficiency of vitamin A causes night blindness because vitamin A is essential for the proper functioning of rod cells in the retina, which help us see in dim light. Without enough vitamin A, these rod cells cannot work effectively, making it difficult to see at night. 26. Color blindness occurs where the core cells of the retina stop functioning. Why? Ans:- Colour blindness occurs when the cone cells of the retina stop functioning properly because these cells are responsible for detecting different colours of light. When some types of cone cells are missing or defective, the eye cannot distinguish certain colours correctly, leading to colour blindness. 27. At present, data can be transmitted at a very fast rate through fiber internet. Mention the role of total internal reflection of light in fiber internet. Ans:- In fiber internet, total internal reflection allows light signals to travel through the optical fiber with very little loss. The light continuously reflects off the inner walls of the fiber, even when the fiber bends, enabling fast and efficient transmission of data over long distances. 28. In endoscopy, colonoscopy and keyhole surgery, how is total internal reflection of light applicable to the devices used to send light to the internal organs of the human body without incisions? Ans:- In endoscopy, colonoscopy, and keyhole surgery, optical fibers are used to transmit light into the body without large incisions. Total internal reflection ensures that light entering the fiber is continuously reflected along its length, allowing it to reach internal organs efficiently, which illuminates the area so doctors can see clearly through small instruments. 29. Mention the reason for the dispersion of light. Ans:- The dispersion of light occurs because different colours of light travel at slightly different speeds in a medium, causing each colour to bend (refract) by a different amount. This separation of colours produces a spectrum, as seen when sunlight passes through a prism. 30. In which case is the image formed by a convex lens real and of the same size as the object? Show the ray diagram. Ans:- A convex lens forms a real image of the same size as the object when the object is placed at twice the focal length (2F) from the lens. In this case, the image is also formed at 2F on the other side of the lens. 31. Will the spear thrown by the boy shown in the figure, from outside the water hit the fish in the water? Explain it based on the real depth of the fish in the water. Ans:- The spear thrown by the boy will not hit the fish if he aims directly at the apparent position of the fish. This is because the fish appears closer to the surface due to refraction of light when viewed from air, but its real depth in water is deeper. To hit the fish, the boy must aim slightly below the apparent position to account for the bending of light. 32. What process is shown in the ray diagram? Name any two devices that operate on this process. Ans:- Two common devices that operate on the principle of refraction are:
1. Lenses (in spectacles, cameras, and telescopes): Lenses use refraction to converge or diverge light rays to form images.
2. Prisms: Prisms use refraction to separate white light into its constituent colors (dispersion).
